chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Guard against the cold in its beginning and welcome it towards its end, for it affects bodies in the same way as it affects trees: its beginning burns and its end gives fresh leaves.

key_terms.آخِرِهِ: Its end (referring to the conclusion of the cold season)
key_terms.أَوَّلِهِ: Its beginning (referring to the start of the cold season)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on protecting health against seasonal cold extremes?
ai.summary: In this aphorism from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the botanical metaphor of trees to illustrate the physiological impact of seasonal temperature shifts, advising protection from the harsh, desiccating cold of early winter and exposure to the revitalizing chill of late winter. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating empirical observation of nature with spiritual and physical well-being, emphasizing harmony with the natural order (fitrah) as a means of preserving health.
